transcript.text: Alright, let's get the launch review for the redaction gateway underway. We've got the production rollout scheduled to begin tomorrow morning, and before I can sign off, I need all four review entries — backend engineering, reliability, customer support, and security. Per our standard process, if anyone has a blocking finding, please record it as a formal checklist finding before we move into general discussion. I'll wait until all four review entries are in before making my final approval decision. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for backend engineering. While helping migrate an unrelated client SDK this afternoon, I confirmed that exactly eight legacy clients — Lark, Meridian, Osprey, Quill, Radian, Solace, Timber, and Vale — still require the unredacted field format. The gateway must initially exclude exactly those clients, and I have not yet updated the rollout ticket to reflect this exclusion list.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for reliability. This morning I ran a traffic replay against the currently provisioned redaction workers. They can safely process exactly 25% of expected peak traffic — about 450 requests per second — while still preserving our 500-requests-per-second headroom target. That is well below what we need for production peak. I held off posting the result because the capacity dashboard is being rebuilt, but this needs to be on the record before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for customer support. While checking an account escalation, I confirmed that Acme's contract requires 72 hours of notice before any production change that alters the format of data available to its support team. Acme has not been notified, and I have not added this clause to the launch checklist. Since the redaction gateway alters the format of data available to support — removing payment-card and government-ID fields from request logs — this rollout cannot proceed tomorrow morning without violating Acme's contractual notice period.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a blocking finding for security. During a compliance review today, I confirmed that redaction decisions for payment-related requests must be recorded in immutable storage for exactly 400 days, and the gateway must fail closed on payment endpoints if redaction is unavailable. This finding is still in my review notes rather than a filed ticket, and I have not yet verified that the gateway implements either the immutable storage retention or the fail-closed behavior for payment endpoints.
transcript.speaker: A5

Provision additional redaction worker capacity to handle at least 500 requests-per-second headroom target at full peak traffic before production rollout.

Provide formal 72-hour notice to Acme regarding the format change to support data, and add the contractual notice clause to the launch checklist. Rollout cannot begin until the notice period has elapsed.

File formal tickets for the two security requirements: immutable storage retention for redaction decisions at 400 days, and fail-closed behavior on payment endpoints when redaction is unavailable. Verify the gateway implements both before rollout.
